title_en: Stories of Modern China (10/20): Two Brothers, Two Paths
note_en: To say how many times something happened, Chinese puts the number + 次 after the verb: 小海换了几次工作 "Xiaohai changed jobs several times." The order is verb + 了 + number + 次 + object, so the count sits between the verb and its object, while in English "several times" comes at the end. The same pattern with 一 and a negative means "not even once": 一次病假都没请过 "never once took sick leave."
